blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land.

items: Article 32 is known as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' according to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into force on 26th January 1950.
Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution.
Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV are non-justiciable in nature.
The Preamble declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
